title: Crystal Lake man sentenced to four years for vape shop smash-and-grab burglary attempt
text:
Crystal Lake man sentenced to four years for vape shop smash-and-grab burglary attempt
H. F. Dowd
Victor Diaz, 24, of Crystal Lake, Illinois, was sentenced to four years in the Illinois Department of Corrections after pleading guilty to burglary, a Class 2 felony, according to an announcement by McHenry County State's Attorney Randi L. Freese on July 22.
The conviction is related to an early morning incident on February 20 when Diaz drove a stolen Jeep through the front entrance of a Crystal Lake vape shop with a female accomplice in the passenger seat. The vehicle became lodged inside the building and both individuals fled on foot without stealing merchandise. Investigators later determined that approximately one and a half hours earlier, Diaz had used the same stolen Jeep in a similar attempted burglary at another vape shop in Bartlett.
Detectives from the Crystal Lake Police Department used surveillance footage, forensic evidence, and advanced cellular data analysis during their investigation. By employing cellular mapping techniques, investigators identified a single device present at both crime scenes as well as nearby neighborhoods at times corroborated by video surveillance. This breakthrough enabled detectives to identify both suspects involved.
Data extracted from the passenger's phone led investigators to confirm Diaz as the driver responsible for carrying out both burglaries. Freese commended Detective Douglas Meyer for his investigative work and use of technology that resulted in positive identification and conviction. "This case demonstrates that criminals cannot assume they will escape accountability simply because they flee the scene," Freese said. "Through exceptional investigative work and the effective use of technology, law enforcement was able to reconstruct this man’s movements and identify those responsible for these dangerous crimes. Smash-and-grab burglaries place businesses, employees, and the public at significant risk, and we will continue to aggressively prosecute those who commit them." She also thanked the Bartlett Police Department for its assistance during the investigation.
The case was prosecuted by Assistant State's Attorney Elizabeth Vonau.
In related context about McHenry County schools: The average student-to-teacher ratio in McHenry County was 14-to-1 during the 2022-23 school year with 45,580 students enrolled across county schools; Huntley High School had the highest enrollment among white students while Harvard High School had the highest Hispanic student enrollment; Harry D. Jacobs High School recorded the highest Black student enrollment; teacher absenteeism rate stood at 34.2%, slightly below the state average—all according to the Illinois State Board of Education.
